claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! Thanks for getting in touch. I'm happy to help you work out if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

To continue assessing your eligibility, could you please tell me: do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, there are some specific circumstances where you may still be able to claim Child Benefit.

Could you tell me a bit more about your situation? Specifically:

Are you a Crown servant (for example, a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted overseas), or are you living in a country that has a social security agreement with the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I'm just living abroad with my work.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. 

To be eligible for Child Benefit, you normally need to live in the UK. There are some exceptions for Crown servants or those living in certain countries with social security agreements with the UK, but based on what you've told me, it doesn't sound like these apply to your situation.

Just to make sure I have all the relevant information, could you tell me:

1. Does Alex live with you abroad, or does he live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives in the UK - he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex lives in the UK but not with you, I have a couple more questions:

1. Who does Alex live with in the UK? (For example, is it a family member, your partner, or someone else?)

2. Do you contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep (such as food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation costs)? If so, how much do you contribute?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum. And yes, I do contribute - I send money regularly to help with his clothes, school things, and general expenses. I contribute about £30 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for those details. That's helpful to know.

A couple more questions to complete my assessment:

1. Is Alex's mum already claiming Child Benefit for him?

2. Do you have the right to reside in the UK (for example, are you a UK citizen or do you have settled/pre-settled status)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, his mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him. And yes, I'm a UK citizen - I just happen to be working abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to give you an outcome on your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 6 years old and lives in the UK with his mum
- His mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him
- You live abroad (and are not a Crown servant or in a country with a relevant social security agreement)
- You contribute £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep

conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**. Here's why:

1. **Residency requirement**: To qualify for Child Benefit, you normally need to live in the UK. While there are exceptions for Crown servants or those living in certain countries with social security agreements with the UK, these don't apply to your situation.

2. **Only one person can claim**: Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any one time. Since Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him, a second claim cannot be made.

Although you contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep (£30 per week, which is more than the Child Benefit rate), this doesn't change the outcome. The rules around contributions are designed for situations where someone who normally lives in the UK continues to receive Child Benefit when their child goes to live with someone else temporarily — they don't override the basic requirement to live in the UK.

The good news is that Alex's mum is already receiving Child Benefit for him, so the benefit is being claimed on his behalf.

If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if you return to live in the UK), you may wish to revisit your eligibility at that time. Is there anything else I can help you with?
